sarah: Heads up — seeing nondeterministic eval outputs on a quantized llama-variant when sequences split across batches. Repro is flaky in CI but local runs sometimes deterministic. Anyone seen seq-boundary seeding issues?

kai: Can you paste the runner command + seed? also batch size / seq_len distribution?

sarah: Runner cmd: `./eval-runner --model=quant-llama-v1 --batch=8 --seed=12345 --top_p=0.95` — failing cases show different tokens after boundary. Logs:
```
[runner] seed=12345 shard=2 start_token_idx=1275
[decoder] refill kv at step=64 -> rng state A
... output: "...orange" vs "...orang?"
```

omer: This smells like our KV-cache refill path in continuous batching. If a sequence crosses a batch border we call `resample_for_tail()` which currently uses the implicit thread-local RNG without explicit seeding -> nondet when workers interleave.

liam: Nice catch. Quick smoke: set `RUNNER_DETERMINISTIC=1` env and run with `--no-interleave` should make it deterministic. I ran `RUNNER_DETERMINISTIC=1 ./eval-runner --model=quant-llama-v1 --batch=8 --seed=12345` and outputs matched across runs.

sarah: Confirmed `RUNNER_DETERMINISTIC=1` fixes it locally. CI still flaky because the CI job uses autoscaling and `--autoscale` == true there.

kai: We should add a unit test in `tests/eval/seq_boundary_test.py` that simulates partial sequences and asserts identical outputs with a fixed seed. Also add a CI guard: fail on nondet for the eval-suite on PR.

omer: I'll open a PR to explicitly seed the sampler inside `resample_for_tail()` and add the test. cc @liam for the CI job change. PR ETA EOD.

eval-bot: CI run #4827: flaky-evals job failed (2/10) — logs: https://ci.redwood/4827/logs

liam: Thanks. Also add tokenizer version to eval metadata — older tokenizers can split differently and look like nondet. Add `tokenizer_version` and runner flags to artifacts so we can correlate.

sarah: Agree. I'll add `tokenizer_version` and `runner_flags` to eval artifacts and update the eval-runner docs. Thanks everyone :raised_hands:
